lead: One of the most beautiful works of European civil Gothic. Declared a World Heritage Site in 1996, La Lonja was the setting for the transactions that made Valencia the largest trading port of the western Mediterranean.

Built between the 15th and 16th centuries, La Lonja de la Seda was the setting for the transactions, agreements and meetings that shaped the economic destiny of Valencia and the Mediterranean. In the very heart of the city, opposite the Central Market, it still dazzles with its monumentality, from the Columned Hall to the Orange Tree Courtyard.

Its exterior sculptural decoration is one of the richest iconographic programmes of European Gothic: gargoyles, demons, fantastic animals and human figures in curious and provocative poses run across the whole façade.

items.title: Columned Hall
items.subtitle: Also called the Contract Hall
items.body: The heart of La Lonja: a monumental space divided into several naves with eight spectacular helical stone columns that rise to the ceiling without interruption. Commercial contracts were negotiated here and the historic Taula de Canvis, Valencia’s municipal bank, was set up. The spiral columns, without direct precedent in Valencian Gothic architecture, twist alternately to the left and to the right. A Latin inscription on the frieze warns merchants to act with honesty.
facts: First municipal bank in Spain · Today in the Palacio de Cervelló
Latin text on the frieze demanding honesty from merchants

items.title: The Chapel
items.subtitle: Star-ribbed vault with coats of arms and angel musicians
items.body: La Lonja’s chapel preserves its spectacular star-ribbed vault, decorated with heraldic coats of arms, angel musicians and the symbols of the four evangelists. On the central boss appears the Virgin of Mercy protecting the city’s jurors. Its Gothic windows show dragons and fantastic figures, and the entrance door is richly carved with Gothic filigree and the image of Christ the King.
facts: Star-ribbed vault · Decorated with coats of arms and angel musicians
Virgin of Mercy protecting the jurors of Valencia
Gothic tracery with dragons and fantastic figures
Carved with Gothic filigree and the image of Christ the King

items.title: The Tower
items.subtitle: Pere Compte’s spiral staircase without a central shaft
items.body: The tower can be recognised from the façade by its imposing height. Inside is the famous spiral staircase designed by the master stonemason Pere Compte, considered a masterpiece of Gothic engineering: it rises to the terrace with no central shaft, held up only by the interlocking of its own steps. It is only open to visits on special occasions.
facts: Pere Compte · 15th-century master stonemason and architect
Spiral without a central shaft · Unique work of Gothic engineering
Visible from the outer façade of the complex
Only on special visits · Check the calendar

items.title: Consulate of the Sea Pavilion
items.subtitle: The Golden Chamber · Consolat del Mar
items.body: This annexed building was home to the first maritime commercial court in Spain. Its façade combines Gothic and Renaissance elements, adorned with medallions of emperors, kings and illustrious figures. Inside, the Consulate Hall, also called the Golden Chamber, stands out, where the magnificent gilded and polychrome 15th-century coffered ceiling is the great jewel of the space: each piece of the ceiling is different, with heraldic, fantastic and musical scenes from the former Casa de la Ciudad.
facts: First maritime commercial court in Spain
A mix of Gothic and Renaissance · Medallions of emperors
Gilded and polychrome, 15th century · Each piece is unique
Former Casa de la Ciudad of Valencia

items.title: Orange Tree Courtyard
items.subtitle: An oasis of calm in the historic centre
items.body: An intimate, peaceful garden between the different parts of the monument, with perfectly aligned orange trees offering shade and coolness. The Orange Tree Courtyard is the most serene space in La Lonja: perfect for resting a moment before continuing the visit and for contemplating the exterior of the monument’s different wings from a different perspective.
facts: Landscaped inner courtyard with orange trees
Transitional space between the Columned Hall and the Consulate
The quietest and coolest in the monument
Ideal for photographing the exterior architecture of the wings

blocks.title: Tips for the visit
items: On Sundays and national public holidays admission is free — arrive early to avoid queues
The València Tourist Card includes free admission to La Lonja all year round
The Tower only opens on special occasions: check the calendar on the City Council website
The first known bill of exchange in Spain, together with the Taula de Canvis, is preserved in the Palacio de Cervelló
The Central Market is opposite La Lonja: combine the visit and you reach both in the same trip
The full audio-guide visit lasts 60 minutes; with the short version, under 30
